chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: What he does now in Denver
summary: He plays with Ralph Sutton at the Executive Tower and travels to gigs.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well, in case -- there may be something special you want to say, Gus, and I'm keeping you on one track.
No, well, I'm just --
Do you want to stop it a minute and think of anything?
Well, not unless you want to.
(Recording interrupted.)
Well, I tell you what, Gus. Better tell me just what other things are you doing in the last two or three years. I mean, staying here in Denver -- what do you do? Do you go out occasionally?
I go out occasionally. I just came back in, see.
Oh, where were you?
Telmark, in Cable, Wisconsin.
Oh. Did you take a group out, you mean?
I was out there with Ralph Sutton and (Franz Jackson -- ed.) -- oh, it's a guy called Franz, plays tenor, from Chicago. The other two guys, the bass player and trombone player, were from Minneapolis.
And you worked what, a couple of weeks?
No, we just were there for three days. Now I go back for a week, in January, I think, January or February.
Oh, yeah. And there are spots you play here in town.
Oh, I played down at the Executive Tower, and --
Do you take groups in or do you work --
I go in with different groups, like that.
Ralph plays a lot, around, doesn't he?
Oh, sure. He's at the Executive Tower now.
Oh, I see, yeah.
He does the singles.
I see, right.
I've been playing with him now.
Yeah, yeah, I see.
But I go in and out of town, like -- it's better.
And -- yeah, it's very nice, because you keep your horizons liquid and whatnot.
That's right.
Do you get to make any record sessions occasionally now, or --
Not really. Not here.
They don't do too much out here, do they?
No.
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
